cards.text: Paul is writing to the believers in Rome, and he's just told them they're one body with different gifts. Now he gets to what holds that body together. First up: "Love must be sincere."

cards.question: Paul says real love also takes a side. What does it do with evil and with good?

answers.text: Detest evil and cling to good

cards.text: Then Paul says, "Be devoted to one another in brotherly love." Family love, friend. The kind that shows up when you need a ride to the airport at 4 a.m. and doesn't even complain about it. Much.

cards.question: Paul tells the believers to be devoted to one another. True or false: he also tells them to wait for others to honor them first.

cards.text: Next: don't let your zeal cool off, keep your spiritual fervor, serving the Lord. I run ovens for a living, friend, and a cold oven bakes NOTHING.

cards.question: Paul pairs joy with hope and persistence with prayer: "Be joyful in hope, patient in ___, persistent in prayer."

cards.text: Share with the saints who are in need, and practice hospitality. Then Paul turns to the people who make life hard: the ones who persecute you.

cards.question: What does Paul tell the believers to do for the people who persecute them?

cards.text: "Bless and do not curse." Even the guy who cut you off in traffic and then waved at you like YOU were the problem? Yes, friend. Him too.

cards.question: When someone around them rejoices or weeps, what does Paul want the believers to do?
Paul tells the believers to live in harmony and not be proud. True or false: he tells them to stick close to the important people.

cards.text: Paul keeps going: "Do not repay anyone evil for evil." Think carefully about what's right in the eyes of everybody.

cards.question: Paul tells the believers to live at peace with everyone. What does he say about how far that goes?

answers.text: If it is possible on your part
When it feels fair to you

cards.text: Then Paul calls them beloved and tells them not to avenge themselves. No getting even. Not even the petty kind, where you just happen to "forget" to answer their text for three days.

cards.question: Instead of getting even, Paul tells the believers to leave room for God's ___.
Paul backs it up with what is written. Why should the believers leave vengeance alone?

answers.text: The Lord says He will repay

cards.text: Then Paul says, "On the contrary." Not getting even is only half of it. Now he gets to what you actually DO for your enemy.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says that if your enemy is hungry, you should feed him.

cards.text: Feed him, give him a drink, and then the line finishes: "For in so doing, you will heap burning coals on his head." Paul doesn't stop to explain that one, so let it sit with you a minute.

cards.question: Paul's last word on all of it: "Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with ___."
